messages:
maria-finance: Heads up — I found a big negative hosted usage line on ACME's March bill that looks like credits from the March Growth Promo pricing pilot. Invoice 987654 shows -$120,000 under hosted usage. Need guidance on revenue treatment for month-end close (contra revenue vs. deferral vs. period reallocation). cc @adele-accounting @sara-controller
ben-ops: Looking now. Link to invoice: https://billing.internal/acme/invoice/987654. Appears to be a retroactive credit applied to usage lines between 2026-01-10 and 2026-03-15. I see an experiment tag: growth_promo_q1_2026.
ben-ops: Quick snippet from the invoice line export:```
customer,period,product,amount,tag
ACME,2026-01,hosted_usage,40000,growth_promo_q1_2026
ACME,2026-02,hosted_usage,30000,growth_promo_q1_2026
ACME,2026-03,hosted_usage,50000,growth_promo_q1_2026
```
adele-accounting: Important question — was this issued as a credit memo (account receivable offset) or did ops issue a negative invoice line (revenue adjustment)? Treatment differs. If credit memo -> reduce AR / revenue for original period when revenue recognized. If negative invoice line created now -> could be current period adjustment unless we reclass.
tim-qa: We rolled the experiment 2026-03-10 and backfilled credits for eligible customers on 2026-03-20. The backfill script intentionally targeted usage rows from Jan-Mar. It tagged the backfill with growth_promo_q1_2026 and created negative invoice lines rather than separate credit memos (ops decision).
sara-controller: Given backfill behavior, preferred treatment is to trace to original recognition periods and record a period-of-origin revenue adjustment if we can map invoice lines to the months. If not feasible, record as a current period catch-up with clear disclosure. We need numbers by period for the revenue close pack and CFO signoff for anything > $50k.
revenue-bot: Automation note — experiment growth_promo_q1_2026 detected. Estimated gross impact by orig_period: ["2026-01": "-40000", "2026-02": "-30000", "2026-03": "-50000"]. Suggested posting path: 1) Reverse original revenue where tie-out exists (contra revenue GL) 2) If tie-out fails, record in current period to 'Revenue Adjustments' and include memo.
maria-finance: Thanks. Adele — please confirm GL for contra posting and approval thresholds. Sara — close timetable: close EOM 03/31, books locked 04/05. I can prepare the period split spreadsheet by EOD.
adele-accounting: Use GL 4099 'Revenue Adjustments (contra)' for the reversing entries tied to original months. If we can tie to AR/Invoice doc IDs, post reversing JV to the original period; otherwise post to 2026-03 as a catch-up under 4099 and disclose in the close memo. I can approve adjustments up to $50k; >$50k requires CFO review (email to finance-cfo).
ben-ops: I'll export full invoice lineage and attach evidence (invoice IDs, runbook, backfill job id). Job id: backfill-20260320-77a.
maria-finance: Action items: (1) I will produce a period-by-period tie-out CSV + memo (due EOD). (2) Ben will attach invoice lineage & runbook. (3) Adele to confirm GL and approve up to $50k. (4) Sara to prepare disclosure language for the close pack and escalate if needed.
sara-controller: Got it — I'll draft disclosure and queue CFO review if the net adjustment > 50k. Please flag if any customer disputes expected.
maria-finance: One more Q: do we treat customer-facing refunds (cash out) differently from credit memos for R-rec? Adele?
adele-accounting: Yes — cash refunds reduce cash/AR and should be analyzed for tax/withholding; accounting treatment still reduces revenue but supporting docs differ. Note to include refund vs. credit memo splits in the memo.
maria-finance: Perfect. Thanks everyone — I'll post the CSV and supporting docs in this thread when ready. :white_check_mark:
